light.description: A cautious low-light foliage trial for the newly acquired plant. Bright indirect light is a useful starting placement; avoid an abrupt move into strong sun.
light.research: A 30-day Aglaonema commutatum study compared four other cultivars at reported greenhouse exposures of 581 and 1,083 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹; pigment and photosynthetic responses differed by cultivar. Those exposures and brief leaf-response measurements do not establish Alpine Spires’ growth optimum. UF/IFAS separately recommends 1,250–3,000 foot-candles for shaded nursery production (about 13,500–32,300 lux), while describing 25 foot-candles as indoor tolerance. Production, tolerance, and an optimum are different endpoints; neither source supplies an Alpine Spires DLI target.

light.research: An eight-week trial published as Fittonia verschaffeltii used 77.37, 101.22, and 112.38 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹ PAR for 16 hours daily: calculated DLIs of 4.46, 5.83, and 6.47 mol·m⁻²·day⁻¹. The lowest-light fluorescent-plus-LED treatment produced less total dry mass than the fluorescent treatments. Spectrum changed alongside intensity, so this was not a clean DLI optimization experiment. It supports a moderate-light trial but establishes neither a minimum nor an optimum for nursery-labelled Nightly.

light.description: Retains the collection's broad 5–12 DLI trial for the money tree. Favor bright indirect light and evaluate growth before approaching the upper end.
light.research: NParks lists Pachira glabra for semi-shade without a numeric optimum. A 191-day study of the related P. aquatica tested 0.22, 0.43, and 1.30 DLI using white LEDs at approximately 6.7–20.1 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹. Surviving plants sustained growth, but P. aquatica total dry weight and relative growth rate did not differ significantly among treatments. This demonstrates low-light accommodation under those conditions, not an optimal range for the collection’s provisionally identified Pachira cf. glabra.

light.research: A five-week Peperomia obtusifolia experiment compared white-LED spectra at 100 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹ for 14 hours, with greatest biomass under 4,100 K among the tested lamps. Its photon measurement explicitly spans 350–800 nm, so the daily total is not standard 400–700 nm DLI. Separate research on Emerald Isle cuttings recommends 6–10 DLI during rooting. Neither experiment tested mature Obtipan Bicolor or establishes its optimal daily exposure; the existing bands remain collection trials.

light.research: Proven Winners recommends medium-to-bright indirect light for Spice is Nice but gives no DLI or PPFD optimum. light.description: A cautious low-light foliage comparison for this mixed terrarium under indirect light. Watch the probable Hypoestes for fading markings or stretched growth; the lower end may not provide enough light for every member.
light.research: No study establishing a shared optimum for this provisionally identified mixture was identified in the sources reviewed. A nine-week Hypoestes phyllostachya study used 2.7–135 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹ for 16 hours daily. Very low exposure reduced red-purple variegation, while 67.5–135 produced smaller, narrower new leaves: different quality goals favored different exposures. The jar’s probable Hypoestes appears white-speckled, so that pigmentation result transfers imperfectly. Fittonia research supplies separate context, but unidentified fern-like growth and moss prevent a species-based common DLI prescription.

moisture.waterWhen: The planting medium is actually beginning to dry and the plants need moisture. Add a small amount and reassess; the LECA/rock base does not establish an outlet for drainage.

light.research: A species-level Tradescantia spathacea study compared full natural sunlight with 30% sunlight after two years of acclimatization, with measurements in summer. Shaded plants had higher measured net photosynthesis; full-sun plants showed stronger protective responses and more upright leaves. The reported 800 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹ was a gas-exchange measurement setting, not a recommended growing intensity. Neither daily integrated exposure nor a Tricolor-specific optimum was established. NParks also lists Dwarf Tricolor for sun or semi-shade, providing qualitative outdoor guidance rather than an indoor DLI target.
